neighbours.label: the closing quotation mark or apostrophe that ends a quoted phrase (” ’)
fire: The coach told us, “Keep your heads up and finish the game.” Then he left the room.
My grandmother always said, “Never trust a cat that hums.” We still laugh about it.
The sign on the door read “Closed for repairs” in large letters.
She called the policy “a disaster for small farmers” during the debate.
The headline asked “Is this the end of cash?” and readers responded.
He described the trip as “the best week of my life” in his diary.
The teacher wrote “See me after class” at the top of the page.
Critics called the film “a quiet masterpiece” after the premiere.
quiet: The coach told us to keep our heads up and finish the game. Then he left the room.
My grandmother always said never to trust a cat that hums. We still laugh about it.
The sign on the door said the shop was closed for repairs in large letters.
She called the policy a disaster for small farmers during the debate.
The headline asked whether this was the end of cash, and readers responded.
He described the trip as the best week of his life in his diary.
The teacher wrote a note asking me to stay after class at the top of the page.
Critics called the film a quiet masterpiece after the premiere.

notes: Card flags broad (1.3% of tokens at 0.1·max). Peaks: '”' x6, '’' x3, '’s' x2 plus scattered words. Near misses report the same speech without quotation marks.
